passages.text: **Vom 22. Januar 2026**

reference.quote: **Vom 22. Januar 2026**

passages.text: Der Bundestag hat mit Zustimmung des Bundesrates das folgende Gesetz beschlossen:

reference.quote: Der Bundestag hat mit Zustimmung des Bundesrates das folgende Gesetz beschlossen:

passages.text: **Artikel 1**

reference.quote: **Artikel 1**

passages.text:
Den in Genf am 1. Juni 2024 von der 77. Weltgesundheitsversammlung angenommenen Änderungen der Artikel 1
bis 6, 8, 10 bis 13, 15 bis 21, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 35, 37, 43 bis 45, 48 bis 50, 53 bis 54 [bis] und 60 sowie der Anlagen 1
bis 4 und 6 bis 8 der Internationalen Gesundheitsvorschriften (2005) (IGV) (BGBl. 2007 II S. 930, 932), die zuletzt durch
die in Genf am 28. Mai 2022 von der 75. Weltgesundheitsversammlung angenommenen Änderungen der Artikel 55,
59, 61, 62 und 63 (BGBl. 2024 II Nr. 203, S. 3) geändert worden sind, wird zugestimmt. Die Änderungen werden
nachstehend mit einer amtlichen deutschen Übersetzung veröffentlicht.

reference.quote:
Den in Genf am 1. Juni 2024 von der 77. Weltgesundheitsversammlung angenommenen Änderungen der Artikel 1
bis 6, 8, 10 bis 13, 15 bis 21, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 35, 37, 43 bis 45, 48 bis 50, 53 bis 54 [bis] und 60 sowie der Anlagen 1
bis 4 und 6 bis 8 der Internationalen Gesundheitsvorschriften (2005) (IGV) (BGBl. 2007 II S. 930, 932), die zuletzt durch
die in Genf am 28. Mai 2022 von der 75. Weltgesundheitsversammlung angenommenen Änderungen der Artikel 55,
59, 61, 62 und 63 (BGBl. 2024 II Nr. 203, S. 3) geändert worden sind, wird zugestimmt. Die Änderungen werden
nachstehend mit einer amtlichen deutschen Übersetzung veröffentlicht.

passages.text: **Artikel 2**

reference.quote: **Artikel 2**

passages.text:
Durch dieses Gesetz in Verbindung mit den Internationalen Gesundheitsvorschriften (2005) (IGV) werden die
Grundrechte der körperlichen Unversehrtheit (Artikel 2 Absatz 2 Satz 1 des Grundgesetzes), der Freiheit der Person
(Artikel 2 Absatz 2 Satz 2 des Grundgesetzes), des Brief- und Postgeheimnisses (Artikel 10 des Grundgesetzes) und
der Freizügigkeit (Artikel 11 Absatz 1 des Grundgesetzes) eingeschränkt.

reference.quote:
Durch dieses Gesetz in Verbindung mit den Internationalen Gesundheitsvorschriften (2005) (IGV) werden die
Grundrechte der körperlichen Unversehrtheit (Artikel 2 Absatz 2 Satz 1 des Grundgesetzes), der Freiheit der Person
(Artikel 2 Absatz 2 Satz 2 des Grundgesetzes), des Brief- und Postgeheimnisses (Artikel 10 des Grundgesetzes) und
der Freizügigkeit (Artikel 11 Absatz 1 des Grundgesetzes) eingeschränkt.

passages.text: **Artikel 3**

reference.quote: **Artikel 3**

passages.text: (1) Dieses Gesetz tritt am Tag nach der Verkündung in Kraft.

reference.quote: (1) Dieses Gesetz tritt am Tag nach der Verkündung in Kraft.

passages.text:
(2) Der Tag, an dem die Änderungen der Internationalen Gesundheitsvorschriften (2005) (IGV) nach ihrem Artikel 59
Absatz 2 für die Bundesrepublik Deutschland in Kraft treten, ist im Bundesgesetzblatt bekannt zu geben.

reference.quote:
(2) Der Tag, an dem die Änderungen der Internationalen Gesundheitsvorschriften (2005) (IGV) nach ihrem Artikel 59
Absatz 2 für die Bundesrepublik Deutschland in Kraft treten, ist im Bundesgesetzblatt bekannt zu geben.

passages.text: Das vorstehende Gesetz wird hiermit ausgefertigt. Es ist im Bundesgesetzblatt zu verkünden.

reference.quote: **Article 1**

passages.text: **Definitions**

reference.quote: **Definitions**

passages.text: 1. For the purposes of the International Health Regulations (hereinafter “the IHR” or “Regulations”):

reference.quote: 1. For the purposes of the International Health Regulations (hereinafter “the IHR” or “Regulations”):

passages.text:
“affected” means persons, baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods, postal parcels or human remains that are infected or
contaminated, or carry sources of infection or contamination, so as to constitute a public health risk;

reference.quote:
“affected” means persons, baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods, postal parcels or human remains that are infected or
contaminated, or carry sources of infection or contamination, so as to constitute a public health risk;

passages.text:
“affected area” means a geographical location specifically for which health measures have been recommended by WHO under these
Regulations;

reference.quote:
“affected area” means a geographical location specifically for which health measures have been recommended by WHO under these
Regulations;

passages.text: “aircraft” means an aircraft making an international voyage;

reference.quote: “aircraft” means an aircraft making an international voyage;

passages.text: “airport” means any airport where international flights arrive or depart;

reference.quote: “airport” means any airport where international flights arrive or depart;

passages.text: “arrival” of a conveyance means:

reference.quote: “arrival” of a conveyance means:

passages.text: (a) in the case of a seagoing vessel, arrival or anchoring in the defined area of a port;

reference.quote: (a) in the case of a seagoing vessel, arrival or anchoring in the defined area of a port;

passages.text: (b) in the case of an aircraft, arrival at an airport;

reference.quote: (b) in the case of an aircraft, arrival at an airport;

passages.text: (c) in the case of an inland navigation vessel on an international voyage, arrival at a point of entry;

reference.quote: (c) in the case of an inland navigation vessel on an international voyage, arrival at a point of entry;

passages.text: (d) in the case of a train or road vehicle, arrival at a point of entry;

reference.quote: (d) in the case of a train or road vehicle, arrival at a point of entry;

passages.text: “baggage” means the personal effects of a traveller;

reference.quote: “baggage” means the personal effects of a traveller;

passages.text: “cargo” means goods carried on a conveyance or in a container;

reference.quote: “cargo” means goods carried on a conveyance or in a container;

passages.text:
“competent authority” means an authority responsible for the implementation and application of health measures under these
Regulations;

reference.quote:
“competent authority” means an authority responsible for the implementation and application of health measures under these
Regulations;

passages.text: “container” means an article of transport equipment:

reference.quote: “container” means an article of transport equipment:

passages.text: (a) of a permanent character and accordingly strong enough to be suitable for repeated use;

reference.quote: (a) of a permanent character and accordingly strong enough to be suitable for repeated use;

passages.text: (b) specially designed to facilitate the carriage of goods by one or more modes of transport, without intermediate reloading;

reference.quote: (b) specially designed to facilitate the carriage of goods by one or more modes of transport, without intermediate reloading;

passages.text: (c) fitted with devices permitting its ready handling, particularly its transfer from one mode of transport to another; and

reference.quote: (c) fitted with devices permitting its ready handling, particularly its transfer from one mode of transport to another; and

passages.text: (d) specially designed as to be easy to fill and empty;

reference.quote: (d) specially designed as to be easy to fill and empty;

passages.text: “container loading area” means a place or facility set aside for containers used in international traffic;

reference.quote: “container loading area” means a place or facility set aside for containers used in international traffic;

passages.text:
“contamination” means the presence of an infectious or toxic agent or matter on a human or animal body surface, in or on a product
prepared for consumption or on other inanimate objects, including conveyances, that may constitute a public health risk;

reference.quote:
“contamination” means the presence of an infectious or toxic agent or matter on a human or animal body surface, in or on a product
prepared for consumption or on other inanimate objects, including conveyances, that may constitute a public health risk;

passages.text: “conveyance” means an aircraft, ship, train, road vehicle or other means of transport on an international voyage;

reference.quote: “conveyance” means an aircraft, ship, train, road vehicle or other means of transport on an international voyage;

passages.text: “conveyance operator” means a natural or legal person in charge of a conveyance or their agent;

reference.quote: “conveyance operator” means a natural or legal person in charge of a conveyance or their agent;

passages.text: “crew” means persons on board a conveyance who are not passengers;

reference.quote: “crew” means persons on board a conveyance who are not passengers;

passages.text: “departure” means, for persons, baggage, cargo, conveyances or goods, the act of leaving a territory;

reference.quote: “departure” means, for persons, baggage, cargo, conveyances or goods, the act of leaving a territory;

passages.text:
“deratting” means the procedure whereby health measures are taken to control or kill rodent vectors of human disease present in
baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, facilities, goods and postal parcels at the point of entry;

reference.quote:
“deratting” means the procedure whereby health measures are taken to control or kill rodent vectors of human disease present in
baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, facilities, goods and postal parcels at the point of entry;

passages.text: “Director-General” means the Director-General of the World Health Organization;

reference.quote: “Director-General” means the Director-General of the World Health Organization;

passages.text:
“disease” means an illness or medical condition, irrespective of origin or source, that presents or could present significant harm to
humans;

reference.quote:
“disease” means an illness or medical condition, irrespective of origin or source, that presents or could present significant harm to
humans;

passages.text:
“disinsection” means the procedure whereby health measures are taken to control or kill the insect vectors of human diseases present
in baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods and postal parcels;

reference.quote:
“disinsection” means the procedure whereby health measures are taken to control or kill the insect vectors of human diseases present
in baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods and postal parcels;

passages.text: “event” means a manifestation of disease or an occurrence that creates a potential for disease;

reference.quote: “event” means a manifestation of disease or an occurrence that creates a potential for disease;

passages.text:
“goods” mean tangible products, including animals and plants, transported on an international voyage, including for utilization on board
a conveyance;

reference.quote:
“goods” mean tangible products, including animals and plants, transported on an international voyage, including for utilization on board
a conveyance;

passages.text: “ground crossing” means a point of land entry in a State Party, including one utilized by road vehicles and trains;

reference.quote: “ground crossing” means a point of land entry in a State Party, including one utilized by road vehicles and trains;

passages.text:
“ground transport vehicle” means a motorized conveyance for overland transport on an international voyage, including trains, coaches,
lorries and automobiles;

reference.quote:
“ground transport vehicle” means a motorized conveyance for overland transport on an international voyage, including trains, coaches,
lorries and automobiles;

passages.text:
“health measure” means procedures applied to prevent the spread of disease or contamination; a health measure does not include
law enforcement or security measures;

reference.quote:
“health measure” means procedures applied to prevent the spread of disease or contamination; a health measure does not include
law enforcement or security measures;

passages.text: “ill person” means an individual suffering from or affected with a physical ailment that may pose a public health risk;

reference.quote: “ill person” means an individual suffering from or affected with a physical ailment that may pose a public health risk;

passages.text:
“infection” means the entry and development or multiplication of an infectious agent in the body of humans and animals that may
constitute a public health risk;

reference.quote:
“infection” means the entry and development or multiplication of an infectious agent in the body of humans and animals that may
constitute a public health risk;

passages.text: Bundesgesetzblatt Jahrgang 2026 Teil II Nr. 19, ausgegeben zu Bonn am 27. Januar 2026 Seite 4 von 55

reference.quote: Bundesgesetzblatt Jahrgang 2026 Teil II Nr. 19, ausgegeben zu Bonn am 27. Januar 2026 Seite 4 von 55

passages.text:
“inspection” means the examination, by the competent authority or under its supervision, of areas, baggage, containers, conveyances,
facilities, goods or postal parcels, including relevant data and documentation, to determine if a public health risk exists;

reference.quote:
“inspection” means the examination, by the competent authority or under its supervision, of areas, baggage, containers, conveyances,
facilities, goods or postal parcels, including relevant data and documentation, to determine if a public health risk exists;

passages.text:
“international traffic” means the movement of persons, baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods or postal parcels across an
international border, including international trade;

reference.quote:
“international traffic” means the movement of persons, baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods or postal parcels across an
international border, including international trade;

passages.text: “international voyage” means:

reference.quote: “international voyage” means:

passages.text: (a) in the case of a conveyance, a voyage between points of entry in the territories of more than one State, or a voyage between

reference.quote: (a) in the case of a conveyance, a voyage between points of entry in the territories of more than one State, or a voyage between

passages.text:
points of entry in the territory or territories of the same State if the conveyance has contacts with the territory of any other State on
its voyage but only as regards those contacts;

reference.quote:
points of entry in the territory or territories of the same State if the conveyance has contacts with the territory of any other State on
its voyage but only as regards those contacts;

passages.text: (b) in the case of a traveller, a voyage involving entry into the territory of a State other than the territory of the State in which that

reference.quote: (b) in the case of a traveller, a voyage involving entry into the territory of a State other than the territory of the State in which that

passages.text: traveller commences the voyage;

reference.quote: traveller commences the voyage;

passages.text: “intrusive” means possibly provoking discomfort through close or intimate contact or questioning;

reference.quote: “intrusive” means possibly provoking discomfort through close or intimate contact or questioning;

passages.text:
“isolation” means separation of ill or contaminated persons or affected baggage, containers, conveyances, goods or postal parcels
from others in such a manner as to prevent the spread of infection or contamination;

reference.quote:
“isolation” means separation of ill or contaminated persons or affected baggage, containers, conveyances, goods or postal parcels
from others in such a manner as to prevent the spread of infection or contamination;

passages.text:
“National IHR Authority” means the entity designated or established by the State Party at the national level to coordinate the
implementation of these Regulations within the jurisdiction of the State Party;

reference.quote:
“National IHR Authority” means the entity designated or established by the State Party at the national level to coordinate the
implementation of these Regulations within the jurisdiction of the State Party;

passages.text:
“National IHR Focal Point” means the national centre, designated by each State Party, which shall be accessible at all times for
communications with WHO IHR Contact Points under these Regulations;

reference.quote:
“National IHR Focal Point” means the national centre, designated by each State Party, which shall be accessible at all times for
communications with WHO IHR Contact Points under these Regulations;

passages.text: “Organization” or “WHO” means the World Health Organization;

reference.quote: “Organization” or “WHO” means the World Health Organization;

passages.text: “pandemic emergency” means a public health emergency of international concern that is caused by a communicable disease and:

reference.quote: “pandemic emergency” means a public health emergency of international concern that is caused by a communicable disease and:

passages.text: (i) has, or is at high risk of having, wide geographical spread to and within multiple States; and

reference.quote: (i) has, or is at high risk of having, wide geographical spread to and within multiple States; and

passages.text: (ii) is exceeding, or is at high risk of exceeding, the capacity of health systems to respond in those States; and

reference.quote: (ii) is exceeding, or is at high risk of exceeding, the capacity of health systems to respond in those States; and

passages.text: (iii) is causing, or is at high risk of causing, substantial social and/or economic disruption, including disruption to international traffic

reference.quote: (iii) is causing, or is at high risk of causing, substantial social and/or economic disruption, including disruption to international traffic

passages.text: and trade; and

reference.quote: and trade; and

passages.text: (iv) requires rapid, equitable and enhanced coordinated international action, with whole-of-government and whole-of-society

reference.quote: (iv) requires rapid, equitable and enhanced coordinated international action, with whole-of-government and whole-of-society

passages.text: approaches;

reference.quote: approaches;

passages.text: “permanent residence” has the meaning as determined in the national law of the State Party concerned;

reference.quote: “permanent residence” has the meaning as determined in the national law of the State Party concerned;

passages.text: “personal data” means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person;

reference.quote: “personal data” means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person;

passages.text:
“point of entry” means a passage for international entry or exit of travellers, baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods and
postal parcels as well as agencies and areas providing services to them on entry or exit;

reference.quote:
“point of entry” means a passage for international entry or exit of travellers, baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods and
postal parcels as well as agencies and areas providing services to them on entry or exit;

passages.text: “port” means a seaport or a port on an inland body of water where ships on an international voyage arrive or depart;

reference.quote: “port” means a seaport or a port on an inland body of water where ships on an international voyage arrive or depart;

passages.text: “postal parcel” means an addressed article or package carried internationally by postal or courier services;

reference.quote: “postal parcel” means an addressed article or package carried internationally by postal or courier services;

passages.text: “public health emergency of international concern” means an extraordinary event which is determined, as provided in these Regulations:

reference.quote: “public health emergency of international concern” means an extraordinary event which is determined, as provided in these Regulations:

passages.text: (i) to constitute a public health risk to other States through the international spread of disease; and

reference.quote: (i) to constitute a public health risk to other States through the international spread of disease; and

passages.text: (ii) to potentially require a coordinated international response;

reference.quote: (ii) to potentially require a coordinated international response;

passages.text:
“public health observation” means the monitoring of the health status of a traveller over time for the purpose of determining the risk of
disease transmission;

reference.quote:
“public health observation” means the monitoring of the health status of a traveller over time for the purpose of determining the risk of
disease transmission;

passages.text:
“public health risk” means a likelihood of an event that may affect adversely the health of human populations, with an emphasis on
one which may spread internationally or may present a serious and direct danger;

reference.quote:
“public health risk” means a likelihood of an event that may affect adversely the health of human populations, with an emphasis on
one which may spread internationally or may present a serious and direct danger;

passages.text:
“quarantine” means the restriction of activities and/or separation from others of suspect persons who are not ill or of suspect baggage,
containers, conveyances or goods in such a manner as to prevent the possible spread of infection or contamination;

reference.quote:
“quarantine” means the restriction of activities and/or separation from others of suspect persons who are not ill or of suspect baggage,
containers, conveyances or goods in such a manner as to prevent the possible spread of infection or contamination;

passages.text: “recommendation” and “recommended” refer to temporary or standing recommendations issued under these Regulations;

reference.quote: “recommendation” and “recommended” refer to temporary or standing recommendations issued under these Regulations;

passages.text:
“relevant health products” means those health products needed to respond to public health emergencies of international concern,
including pandemic emergencies, which may include medicines, vaccines, diagnostics, medical devices, vector control products,
personal protective equipment, decontamination products, assistive products, antidotes, cell- and gene-based therapies, and other
health technologies;

reference.quote:
“relevant health products” means those health products needed to respond to public health emergencies of international concern,
including pandemic emergencies, which may include medicines, vaccines, diagnostics, medical devices, vector control products,
personal protective equipment, decontamination products, assistive products, antidotes, cell- and gene-based therapies, and other
health technologies;

passages.text:
“reservoir” means an animal, plant or substance in which an infectious agent normally lives and whose presence may constitute a
public health risk;

reference.quote:
“reservoir” means an animal, plant or substance in which an infectious agent normally lives and whose presence may constitute a
public health risk;

passages.text: “road vehicle” means a ground transport vehicle other than a train;

reference.quote: “road vehicle” means a ground transport vehicle other than a train;

passages.text: “scientific evidence” means information furnishing a level of proof based on the established and accepted methods of science;

reference.quote: “scientific evidence” means information furnishing a level of proof based on the established and accepted methods of science;

passages.text: “scientific principles” means the accepted fundamental laws and facts of nature known through the methods of science;

reference.quote: “scientific principles” means the accepted fundamental laws and facts of nature known through the methods of science;

passages.text: “ship” means a seagoing or inland navigation vessel on an international voyage;

reference.quote: “ship” means a seagoing or inland navigation vessel on an international voyage;

passages.text: Bundesgesetzblatt Jahrgang 2026 Teil II Nr. 19, ausgegeben zu Bonn am 27. Januar 2026 Seite 5 von 55

reference.quote: Bundesgesetzblatt Jahrgang 2026 Teil II Nr. 19, ausgegeben zu Bonn am 27. Januar 2026 Seite 5 von 55

passages.text:
“surveillance” means the systematic ongoing collection, collation and analysis of data for public health purposes and the timely
dissemination of public health information for assessment and public health response as necessary;

reference.quote:
“surveillance” means the systematic ongoing collection, collation and analysis of data for public health purposes and the timely
dissemination of public health information for assessment and public health response as necessary;

passages.text:
“suspect” means those persons, baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods or postal parcels considered by a State Party as
having been exposed, or possibly exposed, to a public health risk and that could be a possible source of spread of disease;

reference.quote:
“suspect” means those persons, baggage, cargo, containers, conveyances, goods or postal parcels considered by a State Party as
having been exposed, or possibly exposed, to a public health risk and that could be a possible source of spread of disease;

passages.text:
“temporary recommendation” means non-binding advice issued by WHO pursuant to Article 15 for application on a time-limited, riskspecific basis, in response to a public health emergency of international concern, so as to prevent or reduce the international spread
of disease and minimize interference with international traffic;

reference.quote:
“temporary recommendation” means non-binding advice issued by WHO pursuant to Article 15 for application on a time-limited, riskspecific basis, in response to a public health emergency of international concern, so as to prevent or reduce the international spread
of disease and minimize interference with international traffic;

passages.text: “temporary residence” has the meaning as determined in the national law of the State Party concerned;

reference.quote: “temporary residence” has the meaning as determined in the national law of the State Party concerned;

passages.text: “traveller” means a natural person undertaking an international voyage;

reference.quote: “traveller” means a natural person undertaking an international voyage;

passages.text: “vector” means an insect or other animal which normally transports an infectious agent that constitutes a public health risk;

reference.quote: “vector” means an insect or other animal which normally transports an infectious agent that constitutes a public health risk;

passages.text:
“verification” means the provision of information by a State Party to WHO confirming the status of an event within the territory or
territories of that State Party;

reference.quote:
“verification” means the provision of information by a State Party to WHO confirming the status of an event within the territory or
territories of that State Party;

passages.text:
“WHO IHR Contact Point” means the unit within WHO which shall be accessible at all times for communications with the National IHR
Focal Point.

reference.quote:
“WHO IHR Contact Point” means the unit within WHO which shall be accessible at all times for communications with the National IHR
Focal Point.

passages.text: 2. Unless otherwise specified or determined by the context, reference to these Regulations includes the annexes thereto.

passages.text: **Article 2**

passages.text: **Purpose and scope**

reference.quote: **Purpose and scope**

passages.text:
The purpose and scope of these Regulations are to prevent,
prepare for, protect against, control and provide a public health
response to the international spread of disease in ways that are
commensurate with and restricted to public health risk and which
avoid unnecessary interference with international traffic and trade.

reference.quote: **Artikel 2**

passages.text: **Zweck und Anwendungsbereich**

reference.quote: **Zweck und Anwendungsbereich**

passages.text:
Zweck und Anwendungsbereich dieser Vorschriften bestehen
darin, die grenzüberschreitende Ausbreitung von Krankheiten zu
verhüten, dafür vorbereitende Maßnahmen zu treffen, davor zu
schützen, sie zu bekämpfen und dagegen Gesundheitsschutzmaßnahmen einzuleiten, und zwar auf eine Art und Weise, die
der Gefahr für die öffentliche Gesundheit entspricht und auf diese
beschränkt ist und eine unnötige Beeinträchtigung des internationalen Verkehrs und Handels vermeidet.

reference.quote:

der Gefahr für die öffentliche Gesundheit entspricht und auf diese

passages.text: **Notification**

reference.quote: **Notification**

passages.text:
1. Each State Party shall assess events occurring within its
territory by using the decision instrument in Annex 2. Each State
Party shall notify WHO, by the most efficient means of
communication available, by way of the National IHR Focal Point,
and within 24 hours of assessment of public health information,
of all events which may constitute a public health emergency of
international concern within its territory in accordance with the
decision instrument, as well as any health measure implemented
in response to those events. If the notification received by WHO
involves the competency of the International Atomic Energy
Agency (IAEA) or other intergovernmental organization(s), WHO
shall, pursuant to paragraph 1 of Article 14, immediately notify the
IAEA or, as appropriate, the other competent intergovernmental
organization(s).

guidelines to support States Parties in the development of public
health response core capacities.

health measures under these Regulations, the ship or aircraft

point of entry available to it, unless the ship or aircraft has an
operational problem which would make this diversion unsafe.

passages.text:
|Is the public health impact of the event serious?|I. Is the public health impact of the event serious?| |---|---| |








**Is the public health impact of the event serious?**|
1.
_Is the number of cases and/or number of deaths for this type of event large for the given place, time or population?_| |








**Is the public health impact of the event serious?**|

2.
_Has the event the potential to have a high public health impact?_
THE FOLLOWING ARE EXAMPLES OF CIRCUMSTANCES THAT CONTRIBUTE TO HIGH PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT:
Event caused by a pathogen with high potential to cause epidemic (infectiousness of the agent, high case fatality,
multiple transmission routes or healthy carrier).
Indication of treatment failure (new or emerging antibiotic resistance, vaccine failure, antidote resistance or failure).
Event represents a significant public health risk even if no or very few human cases have yet been identified.
Cases reported among health staff.
The population at risk is especially vulnerable (refugees, low level of immunization, children, elderly, low immunity,
undernourished, etc.).
Concomitant factors that may hinder or delay the public health response (natural catastrophes, armed conflicts,
unfavourable weather conditions, multiple foci in the State Party).
Event in an area with high population density.
Spread of toxic, infectious or otherwise hazardous materials that may be occurring naturally or otherwise that has
contaminated or has the potential to contaminate a population and/or a large geographical area.

**Is the public health impact of the event serious?**|

3.

THE FOLLOWING ARE EXAMPLES OF WHEN ASSISTANCE MAY BE REQUIRED:
Inadequate human, financial, material or technical resources – in particular:
– insufficient laboratory or epidemiological capacity to investigate the event (equipment, personnel, financial
resources);
– insufficient antidotes, drugs and/or vaccine and/or protective equipment, decontamination equipment, or
supportive equipment to cover estimated needs;
– existing surveillance system is inadequate to detect new cases in a timely manner.

**Sind die Auswirkungen des Ereignisses auf die öffentliche Gesundheit schwerwiegend?**|
1.
_Ist die Zahl der Fälle und/oder Todesfälle für diese Art von Ereignis und für den betreffenden Ort und Zeitpunkt oder_
_die betreffende Bevölkerung groß?_| |







**Sind die Auswirkungen des Ereignisses auf die öffentliche Gesundheit schwerwiegend?**|

2.
_Kann das Ereignis erhebliche Auswirkungen auf die öffentliche Gesundheit haben?_
IM FOLGENDEN SIND BEISPIELE FÜR UMSTÄNDE AUFGEFÜHRT, DIE ZU ERHEBLICHEN AUSWIRKUNGEN AUF
DIE ÖFFENTLICHE GESUNDHEIT BEITRAGEN:
Das Ereignis wurde durch einen Krankheitserreger mit hohem epidemischem Potential verursacht (Virulenz des
Erregers, hohe Sterberate, mehrere Übertragungswege oder gesunder Überträger).
Anzeichen für Therapieversagen (neue oder im Entstehen begriffene Antibiotikaresistenz, Impfstoffversagen,
Gegenmittelresistenz oder -versagen).
Das Ereignis stellt auch dann eine erhebliche Gefahr für die öffentliche Gesundheit dar, wenn bisher keine oder nur
wenige Krankheitsfälle beim Menschen zu verzeichnen sind.
Bei Gesundheitspersonal gemeldete Krankheitsfälle.
Die gefährdete Bevölkerung ist besonders anfällig (Flüchtlinge, geringer Durchimpfungsgrad, Kinder, ältere
Menschen, geringe Immunität, Unterernährung usw.).
Begleitumstände, die Gesundheitsschutzmaßnahmen verhindern oder verzögern können (Naturkatastrophen,
bewaffnete Konflikte, widrige Wetterverhältnisse, mehrere Brennpunkte in einem Vertragsstaat).
Das Ereignis tritt in einem Gebiet mit hoher Bevölkerungsdichte ein.
Die Ausbreitung von Giftstoffen, Krankheitserregern oder anderweitig gefährlichen Stoffen natürlichen oder sonstigen
Ursprungs, durch die eine Bevölkerung und/oder ein großes geographisches Gebiet verseucht worden ist oder
verseucht werden kann.
☑
☑
☑
☑
☑
☑
☑
☑| |







**Sind die Auswirkungen des Ereignisses auf die öffentliche Gesundheit schwerwiegend?**|

3.
_Wird Hilfe von außen benötigt, um das aktuelle Ereignis festzustellen, zu untersuchen, auf es zu reagieren und es_
_zu bekämpfen oder neue Fälle zu verhüten?_
IM FOLGENDEN SIND BEISPIELE FÜR UMSTÄNDE AUFGEFÜHRT, UNTER DENEN HILFE ERFORDERLICH SEIN
KANN:
Ungeeignete personelle, finanzielle, materielle oder technische Mittel – insbesondere
– unzureichende Labor- oder epidemiologische Kapazitäten, um das Ereignis zu untersuchen (Ausrüstung,
Personal, finanzielle Mittel),
– unzureichende Gegenmittel, Medikamente und/oder Impfstoffe und/oder Schutz-, Entseuchungs- oder
Hilfsausstattung, um den geschätzten Bedarf zu decken,
– das vorhandene Überwachungssystem ist ungeeignet, um neue Fälle rechtzeitig festzustellen.
☑| |







**Sind die Auswirkungen des Ereignisses auf die öffentliche Gesundheit schwerwiegend?**|

**SIND DIE AUSWIRKUNGEN DES EREIGNISSES AUF DIE ÖFFENTLICHE GESUNDHEIT SCHWERWIEGEND?**
**Mit „Ja“ beantworten, wenn die Fragen 1, 2 oder 3 oben mit „Ja“ beantwortet wurden.**|

_Ist das Ereignis ungewöhnlich?_
IM FOLGENDEN SIND BEISPIELE FÜR UNGEWÖHNLICHE EREIGNISSE AUFGEFÜHRT:

Vorhandensein einer ansteckenden Krankheit ansehen:

reference.quote:
**Anmerkung:** Befindet sich kein Arzt an Bord, so soll der Kapitän die folgenden Symptome als Verdachtsmomente für das
Vorhandensein einer ansteckenden Krankheit ansehen:

passages.text:

Gelbsucht, v) Husten oder Kurzatmigkeit, vi) ungewöhnlichen Blutungen oder vii) Lähmungserscheinungen;

reference.quote:

passages.text:
